newsitem.title: FRENCH GUIANA: France pledges crackdown on French Guiana violence.
newsitem.headline: France pledges crackdown on French Guiana violence.

text.p: France pledged on Thursday to crack down on violence in its South American overseas department of French Guiana after the second wave of riots in the capital, Cayenne, in six months.
"There will be absolutely no indulgence for anyone in the pursuit and punishment of those caught in (violent) acts," French government spokesman Jean Ballandras told a news conference.

"Anyone implicated in these events or in other more or less recent events will be held to account for their actions. There will be no tolerance for vandals, no mercy for those who take the police as targets," Ballandras said.
The latest violence was triggered by a series of detentions, including that of a leading member of French Guiana's independence movement.
Ballandras said police patrols would be increased as part of measures to prevent further violence.
Para-military riot police and demonstrators clashed early on Thursday after several hundred demonstrators blocked Cayenne's main boulevard in front of its central police station.
Ballandras said armed demonstrators fired on police and two were injured. The demonstrators also attacked ambulances evacuating the wounded.
Vandals damaged three shops and set fire to two cars. Police arrested seven and used tear gas to disperse crowds.

Alain Michel, a founding member and spokesman of the Guiana National Popular Party (PNPG), was detained last week and taken on Saturday with four others to the French Caribbean island of Martinique aboard a military aircraft.

He was charged with arson and violence against a magistrate exercising his duty when the residence of French Guiana's state prosecutor was attacked last November in a previous wave of riots in which one person was killed and property worth millions of dollars was damaged.
French officials at the time described the riots as "a deliberate attempt to destabilise French Guiana".
Michel faces up to 20 years in prison if convicted, his lawyer said.

French Guiana, on the northeast coast of South America, is the only non-independent territory on the mainland of the Western Hemisphere. Its economy is heavily dependent on subsidies from France and 23 percent of the population of 150,000 is unemployed.
The PNPG favours independence from France.

The European Space Agency (ESA) Ariane rocket launch site is located in Kourou, French Guiana. The launch of two Asian satellites aboard the 95th Ariane rocket took place late on Wednesday without incident and no violence has been reported in the space city.
